inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden has signed Senate Bill 175, adding a citizenship-document hurdle for new voters in state elections. Calling it narrow doesn’t make the burden harmless: people with fewer resources or less reliable access to documents are more likely to be shut out. This is voter suppression dressed up as procedure—making individuals overcome barriers instead of confronting the inequalities that already limit political participation.
inputs.modified_text: South Dakota is doing what a responsible state should: ensuring that people registering to vote in state elections can document their citizenship. Calling a basic safeguard “voter suppression” turns ordinary standards of accountability into a political grievance. The right to vote matters too much to leave confidence in elections weakened; protecting it means respecting the rules and the integrity of the state’s institutions.
